actionable: The fill-hole GT recipe selects the LARGEST-radius cylindrical face with no concavity filter, so on 20/22 cases it plugged a CONVEX outer face instead of a hole — the adjudicator's gt-mismatch quarantine is correct on 20 of 21 cases.
problem: The fill-hole generator recipe picked a convex (outward-facing) cylindrical face as the 'hole' on 20 of 22 cases, producing ground truths that fuse a full-length rod through the part instead of filling a cavity — volume inflation up to +395% (abc_0300) and face-count collapse up to 682->5 (abc_0201); 20/22 fill-hole cases in the run-003 slice are unusable answer keys.

failureOrigin.whatHappened: _cylindrical_axes returns EVERY GeomAbs_Cylinder face with no concavity/orientation test; _fill_hole then takes max(axes, key=radius) and fuses a bbox-trimmed full-length cylinder of that radius. On real ABC parts the largest-radius cylinder is usually a convex outer boss or fillet arc, so the recipe fuses a rod through the part instead of plugging a cavity. Measured on all 22 slice cases: the selected face was CONVEX on 20 of the 21 quarantined cases and CONCAVE on the one gt-ok case (abc_0128, d=17.0 = stated 17.0) and on abc_0281 (d=37.0, 360-deg span) — a perfect separation between the adjudicator's verdict and measured convexity.
failureOrigin.example: origin, direction, radius = max(axes, key=lambda a: a[2])

whyChain.why: the GT<->instruction consistency gate cannot see the defect
whyChain.whatHappened: RECIPE_CLAIMS['fill-hole'] asserts only {volume: +1, footprint: (0,1,2)}. The corrupted GT satisfies both — volume rises (a rod is added) and the bbox is unchanged because _fill_hole intersects the plug with the input's own bounding box before fusing. So check_pair_consistency passes a GT that fills no hole.

remedies.title: Filter _cylindrical_axes to concave faces and assert concavity in the fill-hole claim gate
remedies.rationale: Measured on all 22 slice cases, the recipe-selected face is convex on 20 of 21 quarantined cases and concave on both cases whose GT is a real fill (abc_0128 d=17.0, abc_0281 d=37.0). A correct fill-hole recipe would select only faces whose material side faces the axis; the current max-by-radius selection has no such test, so it selects an outer boss whenever one is larger than every bore.
remedies.whyWorks: A concavity predicate at selection time (face.wrapped.Orientation() == TopAbs_REVERSED on the cylinder, equivalently the outward normal pointing toward the axis) removes convex faces from the candidate set before max() runs, so the recipe either selects a real bore or raises the existing 'no cylindrical face to fill' error and the pair is never emitted. Adding a concavity assertion to RECIPE_CLAIMS['fill-hole'] closes the gate hole independently, so a future selection regression is caught at generation rather than at evaluation.
applyInstructions: Step 1: in _cylindrical_axes (line 274), read face.wrapped.Orientation() per face and return concavity alongside (origin, direction, radius).
Step 2: in _fill_hole (line 334), filter axes to concave entries before max(...); keep the existing ValueError when the filtered list is empty so unfillable parts are refused, not corrupted.
Step 3: extend RECIPE_CLAIMS['fill-hole'] (line 460) with a concavity claim and assert it in check_pair_consistency, so the gate measures that a cavity disappeared rather than only that volume rose.
Step 4: regenerate the 22 fill-hole cases and re-run the adjudication; expect most inputs to be refused rather than re-emitted, which is the correct outcome.

failureOrigin.whatHappened: The adjudicator's only acceptance path is 'a concave cylindrical face matches the stated diameter'. When stated_diameter_mm is null (the 'Get rid of that big hole' / vague render variant), the match count is trivially 0 and the case is classified gt-mismatch regardless of the geometry. abc_0281's input in fact contains a concave 37.0 mm cylinder with a 360-degree span on the X axis, and the recipe selected exactly that face. remedies.title: Adjudicate fill-hole GT by measuring cavity disappearance, not by diameter string-match
remedies.applyTarget: .mutagent/evaluator/run-003/gt-adjudication.json (and the unversioned script that produced it)
remedies.rationale: The adjudicator's acceptance test requires a stated diameter, but 4 of 22 fill-hole instructions drew a render variant that states none, and all 4 were classified gt-mismatch on that basis alone. abc_0281 measurably fills a real 37.0 mm concave through-hole (88,167.2 mm3 added, 96.5% of the maximum X-axis plug) and its own adjudication record lists that 37.0 mm cavity in input_concave_cyl_diameters — the verdict contradicts the evidence in the same record.
remedies.whyWorks: Comparing the concave-cylinder inventory of input against ground_truth answers the actual question ('did a cavity get filled?') using only geometry, so it is independent of whether the instruction happens to quote a number. The stated diameter becomes a secondary consistency check applied only when present, which keeps the 16 genuinely-defective diameter-mismatch verdicts intact while removing the fail-closed behaviour on vague phrasings.
applyInstructions: Step 1: commit the adjudicator as a versioned script — no script exists in the worktree, so the 21-case quarantine is currently unreproducible.
Step 2: make the primary test set-difference of concave cylindrical faces between input and ground_truth (a cavity present in input and absent in GT).
Step 3: apply the stated-diameter equality check only when stated_diameter_mm is non-null, as a secondary consistency probe.
Step 4: re-run and expect abc_0281 to reclassify gt-ok while abc_0170, abc_0254 and abc_0349 stay gt-mismatch (their selected faces measure convex).

assumptions.text: The volume-delta test for abc_0281 is a strong but indirect proof of the fill; the direct boolean GT.cut(input) returned a degenerate result (2 lumps totalling the full GT volume) on this 139-face part, so OCCT boolean robustness prevented a face-level confirmation.

actionable: abc_0352-thicken armA loss is a real agent semantic miss: armA extruded the bounding-box cross-section instead of the +X face profile, adding 24,179.32 mm3 (+66%) of extra material, and its own verify passed because it only checked the three extents.
problem: armA's thicken output on abc_0352 is a strict superset of ground truth by 24,179.32 mm3 (60,996.52 vs 36,817.20 mm3, +65.7%) because it extruded a full bounding-box rectangle rather than the +X face profile — and armA's self-verification reported 'intent: pass' because it compared only the three bbox extents, which match GT exactly (60.100 / 60.155 / 38.494 mm).

failureOrigin.whatHappened: The instruction says to add 12.02 mm of material ON THE +X-FACING FACE. The GT recipe _thicken does exactly that: shape.fuse(bd.extrude(face, requested)) — it extrudes the selected planar face's own profile. armB's script did the same (extrude(target_face, amount=12.02)) and its output is bit-for-bit equivalent to GT (vol 36,817.20, 31 faces, GT-minus-armB = 0.00 and armB-minus-GT = 0.00), scoring 1.0. armA instead built Box(12.02, bb.size.Y, bb.size.Z) — a full rectangular slab spanning the entire bounding-box cross-section — and fused it, giving vol 60,996.52 with GT-minus-armA = 0.00 (strict superset) and armA-minus-GT = 24,179.32 mm3. armA then ran a verify that checked X extent 48.08->60.1, Y unchanged, Z unchanged and surface-type counts, all of which a too-large slab satisfies, and reported 'intent: pass'.
failureOrigin.example: pad = Box(pad_dx, bb.size.Y, bb.size.Z)  # armA — vs — boss = extrude(target_face, amount=12.02)  # armB

whyChain.whatHappened: armA fully contains GT and adds 24,179.32 mm3 on top — exactly the void between the +X face silhouette and its bounding rectangle, swept 12.02 mm

whyChain.why: armA's verify could not detect it
whyChain.whatHappened: the intent check enumerated X extent 48.08->60.1, Y extent unchanged 60.154576, Z extent unchanged 38.494010 and surface-type counts. All three extents are identical between armA and GT, so an extent-only intent check is structurally incapable of catching a cross-section error; there is no volume, mass-delta or added-region-profile assertion in the loop.

remedies.title: Add an added-volume / added-region assertion to the armA verify loop
remedies.rationale: armA's verify reported 'intent: pass' on an output carrying 65.7% more material than ground truth. The trace shows the check enumerated only the three extents, and armA's slab matches GT on all three (60.100 / 60.155 / 38.494 mm), so the pass was structurally guaranteed rather than earned. armB, which extruded the face profile, produced volume 36,817.20 mm3 identical to GT — showing the correct operation was available and expressible.
remedies.whyWorks: For an 'add material on face F' instruction the added region must be the sweep of F's own profile; asserting that the added volume equals face.area * amount (within tolerance) fails immediately on a bbox slab because the bounding rectangle's area strictly exceeds the face area for any non-rectangular face. The assertion fires before export, so the wrong-cross-section class of error is caught in the agent's own loop rather than at scoring.
applyInstructions: Step 1: in the verify step for extrude/pad operations, measure added volume as vol(result) - vol(input).
Step 2: assert added volume equals target_face.area * amount within the part's geometric tolerance; fail the round when it does not.
Step 3: prefer extrude(target_face, amount) over constructing a Box from bounding-box extents whenever the instruction names a face.
Step 4: keep the existing extent checks as a secondary assertion — they are necessary but demonstrably not sufficient.

actionable: abc_0356-boss-union armA loss is a placement miss on a genuinely ambiguous instruction: armA centred the boss on the top-face centroid (Y=19.35) while GT uses the bbox footprint centre (Y=35.28), a 15.93 mm offset — and the vague render variant states no coordinates.
problem: armA placed a dimensionally-perfect boss (r=12.869, h=8.97, volume identical to GT at 13,985.60 mm3, face count 53 in both) 15.93 mm off in Y from ground truth — 1.24x the boss radius, so the two discs barely overlap — because the instruction drew the vague render variant 'Stick a round pad on top in the middle', which states no X/Y while the recipe's 'middle' is the bounding-box footprint centre.

failureOrigin.whatHappened: _boss_union computes cx = bbox.min.X + bbox.size.X/2 and cy = bbox.min.Y + bbox.size.Y/2, giving the GT boss axis at (0.000, 35.278) — confirmed by measuring the r=12.869 cylindrical face in ground_truth.step. armB used the same bbox-centre construction and matched exactly (boss axis 0.000, 35.28; volume 13,985.60; score 1.0). armA instead identified the top planar face at z=8.128 and used its centroid (0.00006, 19.3484), producing a boss at axis (0.000, 19.35) — a 15.93 mm Y displacement. armA's boss is otherwise exact: same radius, same height, same z-base 8.128, and total volume equal to GT to two decimals. The instruction it received was the vague variant that omits the coordinates the verbose variant would have supplied ('centred at X={x} mm, Y={y} mm'), so 'in the middle' is ambiguous between the top face's centroid and the footprint centre and armA's reading is defensible.
failureOrigin.example: Stick a round pad on top in the middle — roughly 25.738 mm across and 8.97 mm tall.

whyChain.whatHappened: the 15.93 mm offset exceeds the 12.869 mm radius, so armA's boss occupies material where GT has none and omits material where GT has some — a double penalty, whereas the unedited input is merely missing the boss once. The score is a correct ordering, not a scorer bug.

whyChain.why: the instruction the case shipped states no coordinates
whyChain.whatHappened: the boss-union recipe renders three phrasings; the verbose one states 'centred at X={x} mm, Y={y} mm' from the same params dict the GT was built from, but abc_0356 drew the vague variant 'Stick a round pad on top in the middle', which drops the x and y the answer key depends on. The recipe defines 'middle' as the bbox footprint centre; nothing in the shipped sentence says so.

remedies.title: Restrict vague render variants to recipes whose answer key does not depend on the dropped parameter
remedies.rationale: abc_0356's ground truth is uniquely determined by an X/Y the shipped sentence never states. armA produced a boss identical to GT in radius (12.869), height (8.97), z-base (8.128) and total volume (13,985.60 mm3) and differed only in Y placement — it satisfied every constraint the instruction actually expressed, and still scored the floor. The same recipe's verbose variant does state 'centred at X={x} mm, Y={y} mm', so the information exists and was discarded at render time.
remedies.whyWorks: Gating the vague variants on whether the recipe's claim table marks any rendered parameter as answer-key-determining means a case can only ship a phrasing that is sufficient to reconstruct its own ground truth. The ambiguity is removed at generation, so no scoring or agent change is needed and the vague phrasings remain available for recipes (such as through-hole) whose GT is fully determined by the geometry.
applyInstructions: Step 1: mark, per recipe in RECIPE_CLAIMS (line 457), which rendered params are answer-key-determining — for boss-union that is x and y as well as diameter and height.
Step 2: in _render, reject a phrasing variant that omits any answer-key-determining param for that recipe.
Step 3: alternatively, keep the vague variants and define 'in the middle' in the recipe description so the placement convention is stated once and consistently.
Step 4: audit the other vague-variant cases in the slice for the same class of dropped-parameter ambiguity.
